title: Design token & component stewardship: contribution guidelines, review checklist, RFC flow, and deprecation pathway
creator: Asha Patel
description: Purpose: establish a single, pragmatic set of rules for contributing to Redwood's design token set and component library (buttons, tables, charts, and ancillary primitives). This ticket delivers: contribution guidelines, a PR review checklist that covers visual/functional/accessibility/perf concerns, an RFC process for breaking changes, and a clear deprecation pathway that minimizes customer disruption. Scope: tokens (semantic + raw), core components (buttons, inputs, tables), data viz primitives (charts), and documentation/Storybook assets. Out of scope: platform infra changes to runtime serving or Dedicated infra (handled by ENG tickets). Goals: reduce unreviewed regressions in production UIs, make deprecations predictable, automate as much migration work as possible, and give PM/Eng/design clear decision points for compatibility trade-offs.
review_checklist: Token changes: follow token-schema.json; include semantic alias and migration note
Naming: use agreed prefix patterns (sys- for system tokens, ui- for component-level tokens)
Theming: ensure new/changed tokens work in both light/dark and High Contrast modes
Accessibility: color contrast meets AA at minimum for text; interactive elements meet 4.5:1 where applicable
Behavior: responsive rules documented and tested (mobile/tablet/desktop)
Docs: Storybook stories updated with knobs/controls and migration example
Visual regression: Percy/Chromatic snapshots added for key states
Unit/Integration: relevant tests and eslint/stylelint rules pass
Performance: confirm no measurable bundle-size regression or render jank for charts/tables
Cross-team impact: list product owners and verify no downstream breaking changes
Changelog: include summary, rationale, migration steps, and deprecation window if applicable
PR size: if large, split into design token -> component -> docs PRs and link them
rfc_process: When to file: any change that can break consumers (token rename/remove, prop removal, behavioral changes in tables/charts)
Template: use docs/RFC-template.md in design repo (link in attachments)
Submit: author opens RFC as a Markdown PR in the design RFCs folder and adds 'rfc' label
Review window: 7 business days for observational feedback; 14 business days if cross-team migration required
Decision body: design stewardship panel + one engineering owner + PM sponsor must sign off
Outcomes: Approve / Request Changes / Reject; record outcome in RFC PR and link to Linear ticket
Post-approval: create a linear issue for implementation, schedule deprecation announcements and codemod work
deprecation_policy: Announcement: public deprecation note published on design console and internal changelog at least two weeks before RFC decision
Token deprecation: 90-day minimum notice with semantic aliasing when possible; encourage using aliased token for 90-day window
Component deprecation: 6-month minimum notice for major API changes; provide compatibility layer where feasible
Chart primitives: 6-month window and versioned chart packages for large API churn
Minor removals: if usage telemetry indicates zero consumers, a shorter grace period may be used with cross-team approval
Migration support: provide codemods, Storybook migration examples, and at least one design-implemented replacement pattern
Enforcement: CI will warn on removed tokens/props for the deprecation window and error after the end of the window
Communication cadence: announcement -> weekly reminders -> final removal notice 7 days before removal
migration_tools: Internal script: scripts/token-usage-report.sh (runs in infra CI to surface top consumers)
Docs: docs/migrations/token-migration-guide.md in Confluence (link in attachments)
owner_rotation: Stewardship panel of 4 (2 designers, 1 eng maintainer, 1 PM) rotates quarterly. Each quarter one steward is the point-of-contact for urgent decisions; rotation schedule lives in design/team-calendar.md

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Large existing surface area of tokens -> accidental breakage. Mitigation: automated usage report + codemods + CI warnings.
Risk: Teams ignore deprecation notices. Mitigation: require PM sign-off on exceptions and publish weekly reminders and a removal calendar.
Risk: Visual regressions after token changes. Mitigation: require visual snapshots and baseline approval before merge.
